opti-1: Night over Florida. Millions of homes glow below.
opti-2: Every day, those homes throw things away. Where does it all go?
opti-4: Much of it is buried in a landfill, layer after layer.
opti-5: This grassy hill in Virginia is trash under soil. It opened as a park in 1974.
opti-6: But some trash never has to be buried. These cans become new cans.
opti-7: So what can we do to care for nature? And which actions matter most?
24-02-welcome: Our film starts in space and lands on a mountain made of trash. First, inspect a giant block of something squashed.
24-02-lesson: Today you're a conservation scientist. Follow a can, test two garden beds, then dig down through a landfill.
24-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
24-02-assign: Time to show what you learned. Sort some actions, then tell us which one you'd choose and why.
how-24-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the block, then tap three things you notice.
how-24-02-compare: Put the lamp under one tray and the water under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-24-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the place shows.
how-24-02-det: Pick three actions, one at a time. Tap a clue, then pick its kind. Predict who it helps most, and watch the place appear.
how-24-02-partc: Draw one conservation action and what it does for the environment. Label the action and the resource it protects, and one living thing that benefits.
